title: Paint-booth airflow interlock with purge dwell
nl_spec: A spray paint booth must prove exhaust airflow before spraying is allowed. The exhaust fan runs whenever the operator commands it (FanCmd) and the system is healthy. AirflowProven is a differential-pressure switch (TRUE = airflow proven). Spraying may be enabled only after the exhaust fan has been running with airflow proven continuously for a purge dwell PURGE_TIME = 4 seconds, and only while SprayRequest, the exhaust fan and airflow are all present. SprayEnable must never be asserted without the exhaust fan running and airflow proven. EStop is normally-closed (TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated); when activated the exhaust fan and spray enable both drop. Use one TON. Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named paint_booth with inputs SprayRequest, FanCmd, AirflowProven, EStop and outputs ExhaustFan, SprayEnable.

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: On emergency stop, both the exhaust fan and spray enable are off.
Spray is never enabled without the exhaust fan running.
Spray is never enabled without proven airflow.
Positive obligation: while healthy and commanded, the exhaust fan runs.
Spray is never enabled without an active spray request.

scenarios.description: Purge dwell then spray enabled on the 4th second
Loss of airflow immediately disables spraying
Emergency stop drops fan and spray enable
After the purge dwell, dropping the spray request revokes spray enable while the exhaust fan keeps running

notes: DRAFT - pending expert PLC review. NEW FAMILY: prove-airflow-before-permit with a continuous purge dwell. Distinct from the existing burner-purge task, which is a one-shot ignition SEQUENCE (CASE state machine) - here the TON is a continuous permissive that must be re-satisfied every scan (losing airflow instantly revokes the enable), plus an exhaust-fan run obligation. Not an on-delay motor start. DOC (reviewer notes applied): PURGE_TIME = 4 means 4 verification ticks under the discrete-time abstraction (1 scan tick = 1 s), not a wall-clock guarantee on a real PLC. DOC: the modeled policy of dropping the exhaust fan on E-stop is a deliberate simplification - plant practice often keeps booth ventilation energized on a circuit that survives a machine E-stop.
